correctness.rationale: For beta>1 the zero-field logarithmic derivative has numerator 2s²+(2-beta)s-(beta-1) and exactly one positive root, giving a global alpha minimum. At epsilon=beta-1>0 the exact Bertin stationary map with s=sqrt D=epsilon sqrt y and scaled drift b=|h|/D=sqrt(epsilon)z/y has a nonsingular even expansion, uniform with three derivatives on compact y>0, leading to F=2(sqrt y-1)-log y-z²/(12y²). Setting F_y=0 gives z²=6s⁴(1-s), unique maximum at s=4/5, so y*=16/25,z*=sqrt(1536/3125). Nonzero F_yyy and F_yz make the local cusp persist uniquely by IFT; no remote/global stability is proved. Independent high-precision solves at eps=.03,.01 yielded cusp parameters trending to the stated constants and checked the height; finite evaluations are corroboration.
